comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS identify the credit card portfolio as a primary driver of their 2024 financial metrics, specifically provisioning and net charge-offs. BAC reports that total credit card outstandings increased $1.4 billion to $103.6 billion, driven by higher purchase volumes. Similarly, GS reports that its provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024, with provisions for 2024 reflecting net provisions related to the credit card portfolio primarily driven by net charge-offs. While BAC highlights growth in portfolio size (outstandings), GS highlights the cost impact (provisions/charge-offs) resulting from that portfolio's performance.

comparisons.peer_topic: Year-over-Year Provision for Credit Losses Analysis
comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.35 billion in 2024 from $1.03 billion in 2023. The 2024 increase was primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio, while 2023 provisions included credit card charge-offs and wholesale loan impairments, partially offset by reserve reductions related to the GreenSky and Marcus portfolio transactions.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures attribute the change in credit-related financial metrics to the credit card portfolio. BAC states that credit card outstandings increased $1.4 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher purchase volumes. GS states that its provision for credit losses increased to $1.35 billion in 2024 (from $1.03 billion in 2023), with the increase primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio. Both companies identify the credit card segment as the key variable for 2024 performance shifts.
